$comment: AI Forging artifact manifest — the single source of truth for everything the plugin
COPIES out of itself into a forge workspace or a target repo.
Why this file exists: /aiforging:setup and /aiforging:update-targets both used to carry
their own hardcoded lists of skills and convention directories. Every new skill meant
editing two commands, and forgetting one meant the artifact installed on fresh setups but
never propagated to existing users — a silent upgrade gap. Both commands now read this
manifest instead, so adding an artifact is a one-line change here.
Paths are relative to ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} (source) and to the scope root (dest).
Anything NOT listed here is never copied, diffed, or overwritten by any command.

$scopes.workspace: The forge workspace root — separate directory (multi-repo), or the repo root (monorepo / single-repo).
$scopes.target: An onboarded target repo root, as reported by detect-project.py (the service-wrapper directory when app_subdir is set).

$update_policies.diff-and-ask: Diff against the plugin version; default Y to apply; back up before overwriting.
$update_policies.offer-default-no: Commonly customized by the user. Diff is offered, default N.
$update_policies.seeded-only: Only files carrying `seeded: true` frontmatter are eligible. Files without it are user-captured and never touched.
$update_policies.create-if-missing: Create when absent; never modify an existing one.
$update_policies.never: User-owned. No command reads, diffs, or writes it.
$update_policies.append-missing-lines: Line-oriented file the plugin does not own. Append only the required lines that are absent (fixed-string, whole-line match); never rewrite, reorder, or remove anything. Idempotent by construction.
$update_policies.rewrite-on-update: Plugin-owned bookkeeping. Overwritten unconditionally at the end of a successful update; never diffed or presented to the user.

artifacts.label: browser-testing — walk testing.md in a real browser, fix nothing
artifacts.$note: Workspace-only: its required input is <workspace>/docs/features/<feature>/testing.md, and it orchestrates across every implicated target. A copy inside a single target repo would be a skill whose primary input isn't in that repo.

artifacts.label: review-loop — rounds of review, triage, and fix across implicated repos
artifacts.$note: Workspace-only, same reason as browser-testing: it fans out across every implicated target and writes its round records into the feature folder.

artifacts.label: architecture-analyzer — read-only advisory analysis pass
artifacts.$note: Plugin-only. Invoked as a plugin skill from the workspace during onboarding and on demand; never copied into a workspace or target. Listed here so the manifest is a complete inventory — a reader should not have to wonder whether an omission is deliberate.

artifacts.label: TDD conventions (Fire loop, feature test suite, harness contract, repository testing)
Playwright frontend testing conventions (optional layer)
artifacts.$note: Only diffed on update if it was installed. Never installed by update-targets on a target that declined it.

artifacts.label: canonical feature-folder convention
artifacts.$note: Not copied anywhere directly. It is the source of truth; templates/docs-features-README.md is the portable mirror installed into the workspace. Change both together — see CLAUDE.md.

artifacts.label: pattern library README (two-tier model, pattern file format)
artifacts.$note: Workspace scope only — the pattern-library README belongs with the shared tier. Onboardings from before the two-tier model also wrote a copy to <target>/.aiforging/README.md; uninstall removes that legacy copy where it exists, but neither setup nor update-targets installs one there.

artifacts.label: per-target .aiforging/CLAUDE.md pointer
artifacts.$note: Render with the target's actual values (workspace path, target name) before diffing, or every target reports a spurious difference.

artifacts.label: seeded shared-tier patterns and anti-patterns
artifacts.$note: Shared tier only. Onboardings from before the two-tier model seeded patterns into the target-local tier instead; uninstall removes `seeded: true` files from a target as legacy cleanup, and update-targets offers to migrate them to the shared tier. Neither ever touches a file lacking `seeded: true` — those are user captures.

artifacts.label: target-local pattern tier (created empty; user-owned thereafter)
artifacts.$note: Contents are user-captured. No command has authority over them — except the README.md placeholder in each directory, which is plugin-managed (see template:patterns-tier-readme). Includes `frontend`: a frontend target that took the Playwright layer has an .aiforging/, counts as onboarded, and can be asked to capture a frontend-scoped pattern — it needs somewhere to put it.

artifacts.label: .aiforging/ANALYSIS.md — architecture-analyzer output snapshot
artifacts.$note: Not copied from the plugin — GENERATED by the architecture-analyzer skill during onboarding, and refreshed only by re-running it. update-targets must never diff or overwrite it (it describes the target, not the plugin). uninstall DOES remove it, because it is a plugin-produced artifact rather than something the user wrote. Listed so both commands can find it in the manifest instead of remembering it.

artifacts.label: .gitignore rules the framework needs
artifacts.$note: Added in 0.3.1 after the first real update run left seven .bak-* files tracked-eligible. The plugin had carried the correct `*.bak-*` rule for releases, but .gitignore was not in this manifest, so nothing propagated it to a workspace onboarded earlier — exactly the failure mode this manifest exists to prevent. In Scenarios B and C the workspace is an existing repo with its own .gitignore, so this is APPEND-ONLY: never overwrite a file the user owns. `*.bak-*` must match at any depth; a rule scoped to one directory (e.g. `.claude/*.bak-*`) misses the backups written into .aiforging/ and docs/.

artifacts.label: docs/features/README.md — the feature folder convention
artifacts.$note: Default Y rather than offer-default-no: this one carries the framework rules that skills depend on (testing.md, the scoped-suite rule, the slice format). A stale copy silently degrades every feature planned against it. Mirrors conventions/features/README.md — change both together.

artifacts.label: patterns/ tier placeholder + two-tier explainer
artifacts.$note: Keeps the tier directory alive — git cannot track an empty directory, so a tier created by mkdir alone vanishes on the next checkout and update-targets re-offers to create it forever. EXCLUDED from every pattern-library glob: hammer-refactor must not dispatch a subagent against it, and uninstall must match it by filename rather than by the seeded-vs-user-captured frontmatter test, which would misclassify it as the user's own capture and keep it.

artifacts.label: anti-patterns/ tier placeholder + two-tier explainer
artifacts.$note: See template:patterns-tier-readme. Same placeholder role, same glob exclusion.

artifacts.label: testing.md skeleton — human QA checklist
artifacts.$note: Not installed into any scope. Copied per-feature by /aiforging:new-feature into docs/features/<name>/testing.md, where it becomes a user-owned document. Listed here so update-targets knows to leave every testing.md alone.

artifacts.label: .aiforging/VERSION — which plugin release these copies came from
artifacts.$note: Written by setup at onboarding and by update-targets after a successful run. A single line: the plugin version the copied artifacts correspond to. Absent means 'onboarded before 0.3.1' — fall back to content inference and say so. Added because the first real update run had to RECONSTRUCT provenance: 13 files showed as modified, most of them user customizations of files the release never touched, and telling those apart took several extra passes. It worked because the run was careful; a less careful one presents all 13 as needing update, the user accepts, and their customizations are silently replaced.

user_owned: docs/features/** — EXCEPT docs/features/README.md, which is the installed convention (see template:features-readme) and is diffed at default Y
.aiforging/patterns/*.md without `seeded: true` frontmatter — EXCEPT README.md, which is the plugin's tier placeholder (see template:patterns-tier-readme)
.aiforging/anti-patterns/*.md without `seeded: true` frontmatter — EXCEPT README.md (see template:anti-patterns-tier-readme)
.aiforging/ANALYSIS.md — describes the target, not the plugin; never diffed or overwritten by update-targets (uninstall does remove it)
.gitignore — append-only; the user owns this file, the framework only adds missing lines
$precedence: An explicit `install[].dest` ALWAYS wins over a `user_owned` pattern that happens to match the same path. `user_owned` is a catch-all for files the plugin never names; a file the manifest names a destination for is plugin-managed by definition, and its `update` policy governs. This rule exists because two such collisions were live at once: docs/features/README.md matched `docs/features/**`, and the tier placeholders (patterns/README.md, anti-patterns/README.md) matched 'no `seeded: true` frontmatter means the user captured it'. Both are the plugin's own files. Without a stated precedence, a literal reading forbids ever correcting them.
